ia_context.current_focus: No accepted modal run exists yet; the project focus remains modal-fit convergence with functional mass already traceable.
ia_context.traceability_note: This file assumes the ENDDATA pipeline bug is closed and uses the valid post-fix A/B as the physical baseline for the next experiments.

geometry_observations.observation: The post-fix A/B proved that equivalent backplane mass now enters the solver, but the modal effect is small.
geometry_observations.evidence: Runs 030/031 produced different BDF and F06 artifacts, with small but real frequency and MAC changes.

geometry_observations.observation: The current target_locations resolved to nodes 204, 302 and 402 on the outer line 12_RIG-V1_yp.
geometry_observations.evidence: Those nodes belong to the rigid/interface-side line and are linked through PBUSH 20 contact springs.

geometry_observations.observation: A better board-side physical path already exists in the model: nodes 1000-2000, 2000-3000 and 3000-4000.
geometry_observations.evidence: Their z-midpoints match the three target backplane elevations almost exactly, while the only offset is about +4 mm in y.

candidate_node_sets.rationale: Best fidelity-first mass-only experiment. These nodes sit on the board-side contact line rather than on the rigid V1 bar line, and the current target_locations are almost exact z-midpoints of these board-edge pairs.
pros: Physically closest to the intended inter-module landing path without adding new stiffness assumptions.
Small, clean YAML-only change; no code changes required.
Keeps the experiment interpretable because only the support-node choice changes.
cons: Still attached through PBUSH 20 contact links, so sensitivity may remain partially muted.
Central nodes 2000 and 3000 carry mass from two adjacent interfaces, which is simple but slightly idealized.

candidate_node_sets.rationale: Sensitivity upper-bound for a pure mass-only model. These nodes are on deformable board regions and have no PBUSH 20 contact attachment, so added inertia should couple more strongly into local/module modes.
pros: Maximizes the chance of seeing a modal response from pure equivalent mass alone.
Cleanly isolates whether mass-only can matter if placed on flexible board nodes.
cons: Less faithful geometrically to a real backplane path because the nodes sit deeper inside each board.
If this set moves the modes a lot, it may represent an upper bound rather than the best physical model.

candidate_node_sets.rationale: Good compromise if the goal is to amplify modal leverage without jumping fully to board-interior nodes. The off-axis pairs spread inertia laterally and can excite torsional/asymmetric content more than a single centerline node per interface.
pros: Still near the nominal backplane elevation and y-location.
Likely more sensitive than a single centerline point because each interface gets a plus/minus x pair.
cons: Still linked through PBUSH 20 contact points.
Includes thin-wall/tray participation, so the meaning is less clean than a pure board-side experiment.

candidate_node_sets.rationale: Simple shelf/tray-dominated alternative. These nodes avoid the rigid V1 line and have no PBUSH 20 contact links, so they provide a clean test of whether the tray/support path is what really governs the backplane effect.
pros: No repeated nodes and no PBUSH 20 attachment.
cons: May represent tray mass more than a true connector/backplane path.
Less direct than the board-edge contact-line candidates.

what_experiment_first_and_why.why: It is the best fidelity-first step. It moves the equivalent mass off the overly rigid 12_RIG-V1_yp line and onto explicit board-side contact nodes, while keeping the experiment mass-only, reversible and easy to interpret. It is the smallest physical change that directly targets the accepted weakness of runs 030/031.

mass_only_pros: Best for isolating inertia effects with minimal modeling assumptions.
Very easy to compare against the existing 030/031 experiment.
Keeps interpretation clean because the only variable is where the equivalent mass lands.
mass_only_cons: Real backplanes are not just mass; they also provide some structural path between adjacent modules.
If the chosen nodes are still too stiff, a pure CONM2 model may underpredict the real modal effect.
mass_plus_rigidity_pros: Adds the missing physical mechanism: coupling/load path between modules.
More likely to affect interface-sensitive modes if backplanes in reality do carry some stiffness.
mass_plus_rigidity_cons: Introduces uncertain stiffness parameters, so interpretation is less clean unless the stiffness is swept in a structured way.
Needs a small code extension and additional reporting metadata.

key_geometric_link.statement: The current target_locations align almost exactly with the z-midpoints of board-edge center pairs (1000-2000), (2000-3000) and (3000-4000).

expected_modal_sensitivity.assessment: Highest expected sensitivity for pure mass-only because the nodes are on deformable board regions without PBUSH 20 attachment.
High expected sensitivity because the mass is spread laterally and can influence torsional/asymmetric content.
Medium-high sensitivity with a clean tray/shelf interpretation and no PBUSH 20 attachment.
Moderate sensitivity, but best physical fidelity among mass-only options.

recommended_experiment_order.objective: Best-fidelity mass-only rerun that directly addresses the rigid-line issue from 030/031.
recommended_experiment_order.decision_value: If this already produces a larger effect than 031, the problem was mainly node choice rather than missing stiffness.

recommended_experiment_order.objective: Sensitivity upper bound for pure mass-only.
recommended_experiment_order.decision_value: If even this barely changes the modes, mass-only is probably too weak a representation for the backplane effect.

recommended_experiment_order.objective: Probe whether lateral spread and torsional leverage matter.
recommended_experiment_order.decision_value: If this moves the modes more than the centerline sets, the effect is likely sensitive to inertia distribution, not just total added mass.

recommended_experiment_order.objective: Alternative shelf/tray interpretation with a very small node set.
recommended_experiment_order.decision_value: Useful as a clean fallback comparison if board-based sets are noisy or too aggressive.

recommended_experiment_order.objective: Move from inertia-only to a minimal local equivalent that also carries a structural path.
recommended_experiment_order.decision_value: Only do this after the mass-only node sweep, so any added effect can be attributed to stiffness/load-path rather than to a better node choice alone.

recommended_experiment_order.objective: Keep the same midpoint bridge geometry and mass, but remove the artificial bridge-local modes before another stiffness sweep.
recommended_experiment_order.decision_value: If the stabilized bridge still improves nothing, the backplane equivalent path is probably not the dominant missing physics in the current modal mismatch.

experiment_history.decision: Localization matters, but correlation does not improve; continue one last mass-only test on a more deformable node set.
Mass-only has enough leverage to move the modes, but the response is not useful for correlation; escalate to mass plus stiffness.
Bridge topology runs, but low stiffness creates three near-zero local modes and is not suitable for modal correlation.
Medium stiffness behaves similarly: same parasitic local modes, poor correlation, no acceptable variant yet.
High stiffness is the least intrusive on the retained global branch, but still invalidates the top-10 modal set with three artificial near-zero modes.

line_b_mass_plus_rigidity_design.concept: For each backplane segment, create one dummy midpoint GRID at the nominal target_location, place one CONM2 with one-third of the total backplane mass there, and connect that midpoint to the adjacent module-side board-edge nodes with two CBUSH elements using a dedicated PBUSH property.

stiffness_sweep_recommendation.label: low
stiffness_sweep_recommendation.why: Puts the local connector flexibility inside the modal band of interest and gives a conservative lower-bound coupling.

stiffness_sweep_recommendation.label: medium
stiffness_sweep_recommendation.why: Still much softer than the existing PBUSH 20 contact links, but stiff enough to create a meaningful inter-module path.

stiffness_sweep_recommendation.label: high
stiffness_sweep_recommendation.why: Upper bracket before approaching the very stiff contact regime already present elsewhere in the model.

why_this_is_minimal_and_defensible: It keeps the current mass target unchanged and uses the already accepted target_locations as the geometric anchor.
It introduces only three dummy nodes, three CONM2 cards and six CBUSH cards plus one new PBUSH property.
It avoids touching global densities, Young's moduli, plate thicknesses, mesh or boundary conditions.

fallback_variant.label: direct_board_bridge_cbush
fallback_variant.concept: Skip midpoint dummy nodes and connect board-edge node pairs directly with CBUSH, while keeping the equivalent mass split over nodes 1000, 2000, 3000 and 4000.
fallback_variant.tradeoff: Less code and fewer cards, but less geometrically explicit and less clean because mass and coupling are collocated on the host structural nodes.

observed_issue_after_first_sweep.statement: All three tested translational-only midpoint-bridge variants introduce three near-zero local modes before the original structural branch.
observed_issue_after_first_sweep.technical_interpretation: The midpoint dummy GRID nodes create a bridge-local mechanism in the current translational-only coupling definition. Stiffness magnitude changes the retained global branch only slightly; the dominant problem is the extra local mode family entering the first 10 modes.

line_a: No code changes required. Reuse the current backplane_equivalent_mass config and replace target_locations with explicit support_nodes plus mass_split_weights.
line_b: Add a new backplane equivalent strategy such as midpoint_bridge or local_bridge in config validation.
Extend bdf_editor insertion to generate GRID, CONM2, PBUSH and CBUSH cards for each interface segment before ENDDATA.
Record the inserted endpoint nodes, midpoint coordinates, stiffness values and generated card IDs in run_manifest.json, mass_summary.json and report.html.
Add regression tests for insertion order, exact mass conservation and traceability of the new local bridge cards.
line_b_follow_up: Keep the midpoint-bridge strategy but regularize the dummy-node DOFs so it does not inject three artificial near-zero modes into the first 10 model modes.
Options to test: add explicit rotational regularization for the bridge node, or replace the current midpoint GRID coupling with a topology that does not leave a parasitic local mechanism.
Do not retune global materials before this local bridge topology is stabilized.

variant_results.label: low
variant_results.assessment: Soft bridge. Produces three almost-zero local bridge modes and drags the whole pairing away from the global branch.

variant_results.label: medium
variant_results.assessment: Still produces three almost-zero bridge-local modes. Less damaging than high in mean MAC, but still unusable for correlation.

variant_results.label: high
variant_results.assessment: Stiffest tested bridge. Pushes the local bridge modes slightly upward and leaves the retained global branch closest to baseline, but the parasitic low modes remain.

executed_experiment_result.best_tested_variant_assessment: Least intrusive on the retained global branch because it pushes the bridge-local modes highest, but still not acceptable as-is for modal correlation.
executed_experiment_result.why_no_variant_met_success_criteria: None of the tested stiffness levels maintained or improved correlation under the current top-10 modal pipeline. All three introduce three near-zero artificial local modes, change the pairing signature, and worsen mean relative frequency error versus the board_inner_centers mass-only case.

midpoint_bridge_sweep.label: low
midpoint_bridge_sweep.assessment: Soft bridge. Produces three almost-zero local bridge modes and drags the whole pairing away from the global branch.

midpoint_bridge_sweep.label: medium
midpoint_bridge_sweep.assessment: Still produces three almost-zero bridge-local modes. Less damaging than high in mean MAC, but still unusable for correlation.

midpoint_bridge_sweep.label: high
midpoint_bridge_sweep.assessment: Stiffest tested bridge. Pushes the local bridge modes slightly upward and leaves the retained global branch closest to baseline, but the parasitic low modes remain.

comparison_against_prior_valid_ab.assessment: Compared with 030/031, 032/033 and 034/035, the midpoint-bridge sweep is far more energetic but in a non-useful way. The added stiffness path does not simply tune the global modes: it inserts a new bridge-local mode family into the first 10 model modes. That means the current bridge topology, not the chosen stiffness magnitude alone, is dominating the result.

decision_after_execution.why: The midpoint-bridge implementation is solver-valid and traceable, but all tested stiffness levels inject three near-zero local modes and poison the first 10 mode set. The right next step is to stabilize the dummy-node/coupling definition before interpreting stiffness sensitivity as physics.

next_recommended_experiment_after_execut.why: Keep the same midpoint geometry, mass target and endpoint nodes, but remove the parasitic bridge-local modes by regularizing the midpoint node DOFs or changing the coupling topology. Only after that should another stiffness sweep be used to judge whether local backplane stiffness improves correlation.
